project.name: energy-proxy
project.description: Home Energy Monitoring & HVAC Optimization stack

nodes.name: arm_calendar.py
nodes.summary: Locked 12-arm A/B-alternating SCED study calendar (2026-06-01 to 2026-11-16, 14-day periods with 48h washout) with UTC-safe hour-index helpers that handle arm 11's fall-back DST fold without naive-CT collisions.
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclass ArmPeriod + module-level ARM_CALENDAR tuple; hour-index <-> datetime arithmetic deliberately done in UTC via zoneinfo to keep arm 11 k=287 -> 22:00 CST.

nodes.name: ArmPeriod
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass representing one arm period: 1-based index, A or B treatment letter, and inclusive/exclusive CT-naive datetime bounds.

nodes.name: current_arm_at
nodes.summary: Returns the ArmPeriod whose half-open [start_ct, end_ct) window contains the given CT-naive datetime, or None outside the experiment window.

nodes.name: post_washout_start
nodes.summary: Returns CT-naive datetime of the start of the post-washout 288-hour analysis window for an arm (arm.start_ct + 48h).

nodes.name: hour_index_to_datetime
nodes.summary: Converts post-washout hour-index k (0..287) for an arm to a CT-naive datetime using UTC arithmetic so arm 11 fall-back maps correctly to 22:00 CST not 23:00.

nodes.name: datetime_to_hour_index
nodes.summary: Inverse of hour_index_to_datetime: returns the post-washout hour index 0..287 for a CT-naive datetime, or None if outside the window or inside another arm's washout/range.

nodes.name: arm_period_pipeline.py
nodes.summary: End-to-end SCED arm-period analysis orchestrator: builds per-hour modes, applies validity gates, computes weather vectors, performs Hungarian matching across A/B arms, then produces per-pair HVAC$/kWh rows, pre-registered bucket summaries, and bill reconciliations.
nodes.languageNotes: Joins are keyed on UTC instants or hour-index (never naive CT) to preserve arm 11's DST fold distinction; rate snapshot is a frozen April 2026 default unless caller overrides.

nodes.name: PipelineResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass return type bundling per-pair table, pre-registered bucket summaries, mode distribution, list of arms that passed the validity gate, and bill-reconciliation rows.

nodes.name: _telemetry_valid_set_for_arm
nodes.summary: Returns the set of post-washout hour-indices in [0, 287] where every HVAC channel meets spec §7's >=110-samples + no-gap-over-120s thresholds for the given arm.

nodes.name: _hourly_mode_from_telemetry
nodes.summary: Produces the length-288 HourMode sequence for an arm by overlaying recorded hvac_arm_mode telemetry on the telemetry-valid set, with TELEMETRY_INVALID overriding any other mode.

nodes.name: _hourly_hvac_kwh
nodes.summary: Aggregates 5-minute Refoss em:2 + em:8 + em:9 power samples into a length-288 hourly kWh array for the arm's post-washout window.

nodes.name: _hourly_rates
nodes.summary: Computes the length-288 bill-canonical c/kWh rate array per hour by combining PJM rt_hrl_lmps with the rate_snapshot primitives and DTOD hourly delivery.

nodes.name: _hourly_em28_watts
nodes.summary: Computes per-hour mean watts on the em:2 + em:8 cooling channels for the arm, used by the spec §9 cooling-active flag (>100W threshold).

nodes.name: _hourly_ct_outdoor_temp
nodes.summary: Aggregates Ecowitt outdoor temperature samples into hourly mean F over the arm's 288-hour post-washout window.

nodes.name: _build_pair_row
nodes.summary: Assembles the per-matched-pair row: applies cost-matched symmetric exclusion, sums HVAC$ and kWh on each arm, computes high-temp / cooling-active sub-buckets, and attaches all spec §9 provenance fields including weather match quality.

nodes.name: _bucket_summary
nodes.summary: Reduces a list of per-pair rows into one aggregate summary row (sum of A and B costs, diff, n_pairs).

nodes.name: _build_bucket_summaries
nodes.summary: Produces the pre-registered spec §9.5 summary buckets (overall, high-temp, cooling-active, low-cooling-exposure) from the per-pair rows.

nodes.name: run_full_pipeline
nodes.summary: Top-level entry point: runs the full §4-§9 pipeline end-to-end across all 12 arms from the seven raw dataframes plus rate snapshot and arm calendar, returning a PipelineResult.

nodes.name: _pivot_long_form_bills
nodes.summary: Normalizes ComEd long-form bill rows into one wide row per bill period, excluding miscellaneous one-time charges from variable totals per spec §10.

nodes.name: _reconcile_against_bills
nodes.summary: Drives per-bill-period reconciliation: extracts UTC window, calls reconcile_bill_period, and collects BillReconciliation rows for each ComEd bill.

nodes.name: bill_reconciliation.py
nodes.summary: Reconstructs monthly variable charges from Eagle smart-meter (canonical) with Refoss mains fallback and flags divergence from actual ComEd bills using the max(5%, $10) threshold per spec §10.
nodes.languageNotes: Strict no-rescaling discipline: divergence is reported, never silently corrected, to preserve HVAC$ defensibility.

nodes.name: BillReconciliation
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass with per-bill-period reconstructed vs actual variable dollars, divergence (% and $), divergence_flagged, plus Eagle/Refoss coverage provenance.

nodes.name: _hourly_kwh_from_eagle_totalizer
nodes.summary: Differences Eagle delivered_kwh totalizer samples into per-hour kWh deltas across the bill window, returning a hour -> kWh dict (only hours with coverage are populated).

nodes.name: _hourly_kwh_from_refoss_mains
nodes.summary: Aggregates Refoss em:1 + em:7 mains 5-minute power samples into per-hour kWh fallbacks for hours where Eagle has no coverage.

nodes.name: _hourly_rate_lookup
nodes.summary: Builds a per-hour c/kWh rate dict over the requested hours by joining rt_hrl_lmps with the rate snapshot and DTOD delivery rate.

nodes.name: reconcile_bill_period
nodes.summary: Public entry point: reconciles one ComEd bill period by summing reconstructed variable dollars across hours (Eagle primary, Refoss fallback), comparing to actual bill total, and returning a BillReconciliation with divergence and coverage provenance.

nodes.name: cost_matched_exclusion.py
nodes.summary: Implements spec §5 cost-matched symmetric exclusion: for each hour where one arm is fully-valid but the other is not, greedily drops one matched hour from the valid arm by minimizing |rate_diff|, ties broken by earliest hour.
nodes.languageNotes: Length-288 lists indexed by post-washout hour-index 0..287; greedy 1:1 with provenance of median rate diff and per-side drop counts.

nodes.name: ExclusionResult
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass carrying post-exclusion valid_a/valid_b boolean lists, median rate match quality (c/kWh), and per-side drop counts.

nodes.name: cost_matched_exclude_with_provenance
nodes.summary: Returns an ExclusionResult with the cost-matched symmetric exclusion applied to both arms plus provenance fields (median rate diff, drop counts).

nodes.name: cost_matched_exclude
nodes.summary: Thin wrapper returning only the post-exclusion (valid_a, valid_b) tuple for callers that do not need provenance.

nodes.name: dtod_rates.py
nodes.summary: Frozen-at-OSF-filing ComEd DTOD (Distribution Time-of-Day) resultant rates plus IEDT, indexed by CT hour-of-day per spec §8 from the April 2026 tariff worksheet.

nodes.name: dtod_resultant_c_per_kwh
nodes.summary: Returns the DTOD resultant c/kWh rate for a given CT hour-of-day 0..23 (Morning / Mid-Day Peak / Evening / Overnight bands), excluding IEDT.

nodes.name: dtod_total_delivery_c_per_kwh
nodes.summary: Returns the full per-kWh delivery total (DTOD resultant + IEDT) for a given CT hour, matching the spec §8 right-most column used in HVAC$ computation.

nodes.name: eagle_coverage.py
nodes.summary: Reports the percentage of hours in a bill window that have at least one Eagle smart-meter sample, used by bill_reconciliation provenance to size the Refoss fallback share.

nodes.name: eagle_coverage_pct
nodes.summary: Returns [0, 100] percent of hours in [start_utc, end_utc) where the Eagle dataframe has at least one observation; handles tz-aware or naive UTC input.

nodes.name: hvac_dollars.py
nodes.summary: Per-hour HVAC dollar (actually cents) computation per spec §4: sums LMP/10 + PEA + transmission + misc procurement + DTOD delivery + variable riders + (negative) CFE credit, then multiplies by hourly HVAC kWh.

nodes.name: HourlyRateInputs
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of all seven c/kWh rate components for one hour, with LMP in $/MWh (raw PJM form) and a typically-negative CFE credit.

nodes.name: hourly_rate_c_per_kwh
nodes.summary: Returns the bill-canonical c/kWh rate at one hour from a HourlyRateInputs, used both for HVAC$ and as the cost-matched-exclusion rate primitive.

nodes.name: hvac_dollars_for_hour
nodes.summary: Returns HVAC cost in CENTS for one hour as hvac_kwh times hourly_rate_c_per_kwh (kWh bucket already carries the 1-hour conversion).

nodes.name: hvac_telemetry_validity.py
nodes.summary: Per-hour HVAC telemetry validity check per spec §7: every channel in {em:2, em:8, em:9} must have >=110 power_w samples in the hour with no intra-hour gap > 120s including the hour boundaries.

nodes.name: hour_is_telemetry_valid
nodes.summary: Returns True iff every HVAC channel meets spec §7 sample-count and intra-hour-gap thresholds in [hour_start_utc, +1h); any single-channel failure kills the hour.

nodes.name: matching.py
nodes.summary: Within-sample z-score on the 4-component weather vector plus rectangular Hungarian (scipy linear_sum_assignment) on Euclidean distance, returning optimal arm-A to arm-B pairs.
nodes.languageNotes: Knows nothing about A/B labels or validity gates; the caller filters arms first and asks for an optimal bipartite assignment.

nodes.name: within_sample_zscore
nodes.summary: Standardizes an Nx4 matrix of WeatherVectors using mean/std from the sample itself (zero-variance columns map to zero, not NaN).

nodes.name: zscore_vectors
nodes.summary: Z-scores weather vectors against caller-supplied baseline means and stds; kept for plan compatibility and sensitivity sweeps.

nodes.name: pairwise_distance_matrix
nodes.summary: Returns the Euclidean pairwise distance matrix between two row-aligned matrices a and b.

nodes.name: hungarian_match
nodes.summary: Runs rectangular Hungarian assignment on the A-vs-B Euclidean distance matrix, returning min(n_A, n_B) optimal (a_idx, b_idx) pairs.

nodes.name: mode_classification.py
nodes.summary: Per-hour mode classification per spec §5/§5.1 into one of {A_ACTIVE, B_ACTIVE, B_FALLBACK, B_DOWN, TELEMETRY_INVALID}, with PJM capacity-risk inputs required only inside the pre-registered capacity-risk window.

nodes.name: HourMode
nodes.summary: Enum of the five mutually-exclusive hour outcomes used throughout the analysis pipeline.

nodes.name: in_capacity_risk_window
nodes.summary: True iff the CT-naive datetime falls in the §5.1 pre-registered capacity-risk operating window (2026-06-01 through 2026-09-30 CT).

nodes.name: required_feeds_at
nodes.summary: Returns the set of input feeds B-active requires at the given hour: always {price, weather}; adds pjm_capacity_risk inside the capacity-risk window.

nodes.name: classify_hour
nodes.summary: Returns the HourMode for one hour given arm letter, telemetry validity, controller liveness, and a feeds dict; telemetry-invalid wins over everything.

nodes.name: is_fully_valid
nodes.summary: True iff mode is A_ACTIVE or B_ACTIVE (telemetry-valid AND in intended treatment mode per spec §5).

nodes.name: run_shadow_validation.py
nodes.summary: Pre-experiment shadow validation CLI per spec §11 #13: runs 8 pipeline-shape checks against InfluxDB for the 2026-04-29 shadow window (ingestion, pricing reconstruction, HVAC kWh, Eagle-Refoss reconciliation, weather vector inputs, arm calendar, mode classification, scarcity divergence) and writes JSON + Markdown reports.
nodes.languageNotes: Influx-dependent checks return BLOCKED with reason codes rather than failing when data is not yet available; exit code maps PASS/WARN -> 0, FAIL -> 1, BLOCKED -> 2.

nodes.name: CheckResult
nodes.summary: Dataclass for one shadow validation check: id, description, status (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/N-A/WARN), optional reason_code, notes, and metrics dict.

nodes.name: ValidationReport
nodes.summary: Top-level run report bundling runner metadata, Influx connection info, and a list of CheckResults with an overall_status() method that promotes WARN/BLOCKED/FAIL severity.

nodes.name: ScarcityDivergenceMetrics
nodes.summary: Dataclass capturing M3 scarcity-divergence audit results: n_diverging_over_threshold, max_divergence_c, plus comed/pjm hour counts and overlap stats.

nodes.name: check_ingestion
nodes.summary: Verifies Stage 1 ingestion is producing rows for each canonical measurement (refoss.channel, comed.prices, pjm.lmp_rt_hourly, eagle.meter, comed.bill) in the shadow window.

nodes.name: check_ecowitt_weather_ingestion
nodes.summary: Validates Ecowitt weather ingestion shape against the canonical ch1_* channels per binding spec §6, including alias-drift sniffs and NOAA fallback station lock checks.

nodes.name: check_pricing_reconstruction
nodes.summary: Checks that pricing reconstruction (bill_reconciliation) yields sensible values, returning BLOCKED with reason code if no DTOD bill is yet available.

nodes.name: check_refoss_hvac_kwh
nodes.summary: Validates that Refoss HVAC channels (em:2 + em:8 + em:9) compute valid hourly kWh and counts cooling-active hours per spec §9 (em:2 + em:8 mean > 100W).

nodes.name: check_refoss_eagle_reconciliation
nodes.summary: Measures Refoss-mains vs Eagle delivered-kWh drift and Eagle coverage in the shadow window, surfacing reconciliation risk pre-experiment.

nodes.name: check_weather_vector_inputs
nodes.summary: Validates the Ecowitt + NOAA-fallback inputs that build_weather_vector would consume, since pre-experiment hours are not inside any ArmPeriod so build_weather_vector itself cannot be called.

nodes.name: check_arm_calendar
nodes.summary: Calls current_arm_at across the shadow window and asserts every shadow hour returns None as expected (shadow data falls outside the locked arm calendar).

nodes.name: check_mode_classification
nodes.summary: Synthetic-input spot test of classify_hour: A telemetry-valid -> A_ACTIVE, B with healthy feeds -> B_ACTIVE, etc.

nodes.name: compute_scarcity_divergence
nodes.summary: Pure-function M3 scarcity-divergence math: at hours where ComEd 5-min hourly mean > p95, compute |ComEd - PJM rt_hrl_lmps| and flag any divergence over the threshold (default 2 c/kWh).

nodes.name: audit_scarcity_divergence
nodes.summary: Queries ComEd prices and PJM rt_hrl_lmps from Influx, runs compute_scarcity_divergence, and returns a CheckResult flagging the OSF risk that controller-observed prices diverge at scarcity moments.

nodes.name: run_all_checks
nodes.summary: Driver that runs all 8 shadow validation checks in sequence and returns the list of CheckResults.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: parses args, makes the Influx client, runs all checks, writes JSON + Markdown reports, and returns the exit code from overall status.

nodes.name: exit_code_for_status
nodes.summary: Maps overall Status (PASS/WARN/FAIL/BLOCKED/N-A) to process exit code: PASS/WARN/N-A -> 0, FAIL -> 1, BLOCKED -> 2.

nodes.name: test_arm_calendar.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for arm_calendar.py covering all 12 arms, A/B alternation, contiguous 14-day periods, hour-index <-> datetime round-trips, and arm 11's DST fall-back collision-avoidance.

nodes.name: test_arm_period_pipeline.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for arm_period_pipeline.run_full_pipeline: builds a synthetic two-arm dataset, asserts PipelineResult fields, validity gating, savings sign, mode distribution, per-pair columns, bucket summaries, and bill reconciliation across long-form/wide-form bill shapes.

nodes.name: test_bill_reconciliation.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for reconcile_bill_period: Eagle-primary vs Refoss-fallback selection, divergence threshold logic, overlap drift, never-rescale invariant, and arm 11 DST fall-back distinctness.

nodes.name: test_cost_matched_exclusion.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for cost_matched_exclusion: no-op when both arms fully valid, symmetric drops when one arm is invalid, closest-rate selection, chronological tie-break, and provenance accounting.

nodes.name: test_dtod_rates.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite pinning the ComEd DTOD spec §8 rate table: IEDT constant, tariff source string, 24-hour coverage, and band-boundary correctness for hours 06/13/19/21.

nodes.name: test_eagle_coverage.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for eagle_coverage_pct: 100%, 50%, empty input, multi-row-per-hour dedup, out-of-window rows ignored, tz-aware input handled, zero-length window returns zero.

nodes.name: test_hvac_dollars.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for hvac_dollars: morning-band computation, zero kWh, negative LMP handled, cents-not-dollars unit invariant, and LMP $/MWh -> c/kWh divide-by-10 invariant.

nodes.name: test_hvac_telemetry_validity.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for hour_is_telemetry_valid: 120 samples no-gap valid, <110 invalid, exactly 110 evenly-spread valid, packed-to-55min invalid, boundary gaps caught, any-channel failure kills hour, power_w field filter.

nodes.name: test_matching.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for matching helpers: within-sample z-score mean-zero invariant, zero-variance returns zero not NaN, external-baseline z-score, 3x3 Hungarian optimal, rectangular Hungarian, empty pool, known pairwise distances.

nodes.name: test_mode_classification.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for classify_hour covering all 5 outcomes, telemetry-invalid precedence, B controller-dead -> B_DOWN, B feed-stale -> B_FALLBACK with capacity-risk window boundaries, plus is_fully_valid semantics.

nodes.name: test_pipeline_end_to_end_arm_period.py
nodes.summary: End-to-end synthetic 12-arm pipeline exercise with -15% HVAC injection on Arm B; asserts all 12 arms pass validity, 6 matched pairs produced, aggregate diff is negative at injected savings, and the high-temp bucket activates above 85F.

nodes.name: test_shadow_validation.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for pure-function helpers in run_shadow_validation: ISO Z formatting, scarcity-divergence math edge cases, overall-status promotion (FAIL > BLOCKED > WARN > PASS), and exit-code mapping.

nodes.name: test_validity_gate.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for arm_passes_validity_gate: 259-of-288 threshold, no 24h+ contiguous invalid run, arm-specific fully-valid (B with A_ACTIVE modes must fail), and wrong-length input raises.

nodes.name: test_weather_vector.py
nodes.summary: Pytest suite for build_weather_vector: 4-component output, CDD sum, nocturnal-min uses 22-06 window with 11 complete nights for a 12-day arm, outside-window rows ignored, arm 11 DST fold still aggregates to 288 hours.

nodes.name: validity_gate.py
nodes.summary: Single pre-matching arm-period validity gate per spec §5/§7: >=259 of 288 fully-valid hours AND no contiguous invalid run >24 hours, arm-specific (A_ACTIVE counts only for A arms, B_ACTIVE only for B arms).

nodes.name: is_fully_valid_for_arm
nodes.summary: Arm-specific fully-valid check: A_ACTIVE only for arm A, B_ACTIVE only for arm B; other modes never fully-valid for either arm.

nodes.name: fully_valid_count
nodes.summary: Counts fully-valid-for-this-arm hours across a mode sequence.

nodes.name: max_continuous_invalid_run
nodes.summary: Returns the longest contiguous run length of not-fully-valid-for-this-arm hours across a mode sequence.

nodes.name: arm_passes_validity_gate
nodes.summary: Returns True iff the 288-mode arm sequence passes both spec §5/§7 rules: fully_valid_count >= 259 AND max_continuous_invalid_run <= 24.

nodes.name: weather_vector.py
nodes.summary: Builds the 4-component arm-period weather vector per spec §6 (cdd_total, mean_daily_max_temp_f, mean_nocturnal_min_temp_f, mean_dewpoint_f) from canonical Ecowitt ch1_* channels with CT-aware bucketing for DST fold safety.
nodes.languageNotes: Drops solar and wind per binding spec; nocturnal-min uses only nights with both pre- and post-midnight halves so a 12-day window yields 11 full nights, not 13 inflated partials.

nodes.name: WeatherVector
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass of the 4 weather components in fixed order; as_array() returns the numpy vector consumed by within_sample_zscore.

nodes.name: _aggregate_to_hourly
nodes.summary: Groups sub-hourly Ecowitt rows by UTC hour and averages ch1_temp_f / ch1_dewpoint_f, so spec §6 hourly primitives are computed against hourly means regardless of source cadence.

nodes.name: build_weather_vector
nodes.summary: Aggregates Ecowitt data over an arm's 288-hour post-washout window into a WeatherVector: CDD base 65F, mean daily max, mean nocturnal min over full 22-06 nights, and mean dewpoint.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Package marker and docstring for the pre-registered analysis package, pointing readers to docs/ANALYSIS_PIPELINE.md as the binding contract.

nodes.name: baseline_distribution.py
nodes.summary: Builds the historical weekly weather-vector baseline distribution from ERA5 reanalysis years, used by Stage 4 matching to score candidate twin weeks. Emits a placeholder file when no qualifying years are available so downstream stages stay reason-coded.
nodes.languageNotes: Streams ERA5 NetCDF per year then folds into weekly CDD / enthalpy vectors; isolates the placeholder emission path so the rest of the pipeline never branches on missing baselines.

nodes.name: pipeline.py
nodes.summary: DEPRECATED single-file orchestrator for the original weekly Stages 1-9 of the pre-registered SCED HVAC study, retained because Stage 7/8 still depend on it while arm_period_pipeline takes over per the 2026-05-13 rebaseline spec. Houses stage entry points, all rule applicators, O2 capacity layers, decomposition, and the CLI run_all dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally a 4.7k-line monolith so spec-locked math primitives stay in lockstep; each stage writes outputs under <out_dir>/stage<N>/ for tar'ing into an OSF filing bundle. Rule applicators take DataFrames in/out so unit tests can synthesize inputs without parquet I/O.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Replay package barrel that re-exports the Manifest dataclasses, source-type constants, ReasonCode enum, and helpers consumed by Stage 1 export and every downstream loader. Implements OSF_FILING.md criterion 14.

nodes.name: manifest.py
nodes.summary: Defines the Manifest contract that pairs each measurement with its parquet file, source type, and SHA256 — the integrity record Stage 1 writes and downstream loaders verify before reading any replay bundle.

nodes.name: reason_codes.py
nodes.summary: Reason-code enum and StageReasonReport schema that downstream stages use to label legitimately empty inputs, so a missing-data outcome is auditable rather than silently zeroed.

nodes.name: weather_compat.py
nodes.summary: Builds backward-compatible weather replay bundles by fusing IEM/ASOS rows with Open-Meteo solar and gap-fill data, then merges the resulting parquet outputs into a Stage 1 directory tree. Used to backfill weather coverage for pre-Ecowitt analysis windows.
nodes.languageNotes: Native long-format parquet outputs match Stage 1's emit shape so the same loaders work without branching on source provenance.

nodes.name: compute_from_era5
nodes.summary: Loads each requested ERA5 reanalysis year, folds it into weekly weather vectors, and writes the merged baseline parquet — falling back to a placeholder when CDD thresholds disqualify every year.

nodes.name: _compute_weekly_vector
nodes.summary: Folds hourly ERA5 rows for one ISO week into the locked weather-vector schema (CDD, mean enthalpy, etc.) used as matching features in Stage 4.

nodes.name: _load_year
nodes.summary: Reads one calendar year of ERA5 NetCDF for the household coordinates, returning a normalised hourly DataFrame ready for weekly folding.

nodes.name: emit_placeholder
nodes.summary: Writes a placeholder baseline parquet with the locked schema but zero rows so downstream stages stay reason-coded instead of crashing on a missing file.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry that parses --out / --years / --min-cdd and invokes compute_from_era5; the canonical way to refresh the locked baseline distribution prior to filing.

nodes.name: mahalanobis_distance
nodes.summary: Computes the Mahalanobis distance between a candidate weather vector and the baseline distribution covariance — the core distance metric for Stage 4 twin-week matching.

nodes.name: hungarian_match
nodes.summary: Runs Hungarian-algorithm 1:1 assignment between treatment and control weeks under a Mahalanobis cost matrix, returning matched pairs for Stage 4.

nodes.name: stationary_bootstrap_median_diff
nodes.summary: Stationary-bootstrap point estimate and CI for the matched-pairs median difference. Deprecated: superseded by arm_period_pipeline; kept until Stage 7/8 callers move.

nodes.name: sced_randomization_pvalue
nodes.summary: Permutation-based p-value for the SCED arm-swap test, holding the calendar fixed while reshuffling arm labels. Deprecated alongside the weekly pipeline.

nodes.name: heat_index_f
nodes.summary: NWS heat-index formula (Fahrenheit) used for apparent-temperature features that flow into Stage 3 weather aggregates and Stage 7 SCED triggers.

nodes.name: enthalpy_btu_per_lb
nodes.summary: Computes moist-air enthalpy (BTU/lb-dry-air) from dry-bulb and humidity — a locked weather-vector component for Stage 4 matching.

nodes.name: dtod_delivery_rate_for_hour_ct
nodes.summary: Returns the locked ComEd DTOD delivery-rate piece for a given CT hour, used when reconstructing all-in retail price for analysis.

nodes.name: weekly_cdd
nodes.summary: Sums daily cooling-degree-days into a weekly total — the primary intensity feature for $/CDD and kWh/CDD outcomes.

nodes.name: weekly_mean_enthalpy_btu_lb
nodes.summary: Aggregates hourly enthalpy into a weekly mean for the locked weather-vector schema.

nodes.name: weekly_dollars_per_cdd
nodes.summary: Computes $/CDD weekly outcome. Deprecated by arm_period_pipeline per the 2026-05-13 rebaseline; do not add new callers.

nodes.name: comfortnet_kw
nodes.summary: Derives ComfortNet HVAC kW from a parsed sample row, used by Stage 1 imputation when Refoss has a measurement gap.

nodes.name: _split_value_column_by_type
nodes.summary: Splits an Influx long-format value column into the canonical schema columns by inferred type so Stage 1 export can write a single typed parquet per measurement.

nodes.name: _write_stage1_export
nodes.summary: Writes the full set of per-measurement parquet files plus the run manifest under stage1/, hashing each file for the replay contract.

nodes.name: stage1_extract
nodes.summary: Stage 1 entry: pulls every required measurement from InfluxDB for the configured window and writes the locked replay bundle (long-format parquet + manifest) under stage1/.

nodes.name: _apply_rules_for_week
nodes.summary: Runs every Stage 2 data-quality rule (Refoss, ComfortNet, Ecowitt, scheduler, PJM, price, forecast, overrides, transition) over a single ISO week and returns the merged RuleResult set.

nodes.name: stage2_quality
nodes.summary: Stage 2 entry: iterates ISO weeks, loads stage1 inputs, applies all data-quality rules, and writes the qualified-weeks CSV with per-rule diagnostics consumed by Stages 3-8.

nodes.name: _load_week_inputs_from_stage1
nodes.summary: Reads the Stage 1 parquet bundle for one ISO week and projects each measurement into the in-memory DataFrames consumed by the rule applicators.

nodes.name: rule1_refoss_apply
nodes.summary: Stage 2 Rule 1 applicator: runs Refoss gap analysis over a week and emits the gap-intervals plus impute decisions used to qualify the week.

nodes.name: rule2_comfortnet_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 2 applicator: scores ComfortNet daily downtime minutes against the spec threshold to qualify or disqualify the week.

nodes.name: rule3_price_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 3 applicator: enforces hourly-price-observation coverage from the ComEd 5-min stream so Stage 3 retail-cost columns are reconstructable.

nodes.name: rule4_forecast_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 4 applicator: checks NWS forecast issuance coverage required for the scheduler's day-ahead inputs.

nodes.name: rule5_ecowitt_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 5 applicator: enforces Ecowitt daily missing-hours coverage on the canonical ch1_* outdoor channels per binding spec §6.

nodes.name: rule6_pjm_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 6 applicator: verifies PJM 5CP-risk inputs are present for the capacity year.

nodes.name: rule7_scheduler_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 7 applicator: detects hvac-scheduler outages overlapping control-relevant windows so a hardware silence does not get scored as a treatment effect.

nodes.name: rule8_pi_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 8 applicator: PI controller diagnostic for the week's scheduler decisions, surfacing setpoint vs realized error patterns.

nodes.name: rule9_overrides_apply
nodes.summary: Rule 9 applicator: classifies manual thermostat overrides observed in the week so override-heavy weeks can be filtered or held aside.

nodes.name: rule10_transition_apply

nodes.name: thermal_observer.py
nodes.summary: Pure-Python thermal response model for the HVAC scheduler: defines ThermalSample/ThermalInterval/FitConfig/ThermalFitResult dataclasses and fits a least-squares envelope model (tau hours, stage-1/stage-2 cooling rates, solar coupling) with rigorous rejection rules (skill-score vs persistence, min stage samples, plausibility bounds).
nodes.languageNotes: Frozen dataclasses + numpy lstsq; no I/O — keeps the fit pure so unit tests can synthesize samples without Influx.

nodes.name: thermal_observer_influx.py
nodes.summary: InfluxDB adapter for the thermal observer: builds the Flux query joining ecowitt weather and HVAC telemetry, and converts raw rows into ThermalSample objects with setpoint-change detection (>=0.5 F).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses json.dumps to safely quote Flux string literals and a regex-validated field accessor to avoid Flux injection.

nodes.summary: Operator-facing CLI that pulls the last N days of HVAC + ecowitt telemetry from InfluxDB, runs the pure thermal_observer fit, and prints a summary; strictly read-only (--output-json is a deprecated no-op).

nodes.name: test_thermal_observer_influx.py
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the InfluxDB adapter: validates rows_to_samples conversion, skip-on-missing-telemetry behavior, half-degree setpoint-change marking, and that build_query references the configured weather measurement and HVAC fields.

nodes.name: test_fit_thermal_observer_cli.py
nodes.summary: CLI integration test for fit_thermal_observer: stubs InfluxDBClient with a FailingWriteApi to assert the operator entry point is strictly read-only and never invokes write_api, exercising the full argparse + query + fit + summary path with synthetic rows.
nodes.languageNotes: FailingWriteApi pattern guards the binding spec rule that the fit CLI must never mutate Influx.

nodes.name: ThermalSample
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass for a single point-in-time thermal observation (indoor/outdoor F, solar W/m2, cool/heat actual %, cool setpoint, setpoint-changed flag).

nodes.name: ThermalInterval
nodes.summary: Frozen dataclass representing a consolidated sample-to-sample interval with stage flags; exposes indoor_delta_f_per_hr and envelope_delta_f properties used by the design matrix.

nodes.name: FitConfig
nodes.summary: Frozen-dataclass tuning knobs for the thermal fit: sample cadence, stage-1/stage-2 duty-cycle thresholds, min sample counts, skill threshold, setpoint mask minutes, and tau / stage-2 cooling plausibility bounds.

nodes.name: ThermalFitResult
nodes.summary: Frozen-dataclass fit output: tau, per-stage cooling rates, solar coupling, RMSE/persistence/skill, filter counts, fit window, and accepted flag plus structured rejection_reasons; serializable via to_json_dict.

nodes.name: build_intervals
nodes.summary: Pairs consecutive samples into intervals, dropping rows for time gaps beyond max_gap_factor, the setpoint_mask_minutes window after a setpoint change, mid-interval stage transitions, and non-finite HVAC controls; returns intervals plus per-reason filter counts.

nodes.name: fit_thermal_response
nodes.summary: Core fit: builds intervals, holds out the last 20% for testing, solves np.linalg.lstsq on the envelope/stage-1/stage-2/solar design matrix, evaluates skill vs persistence, and applies plausibility rules (tau range, stage2 cooling >= stage1, stage-2 sample count) to produce an accepted/rejected ThermalFitResult with reason codes.

nodes.name: _rejected
nodes.summary: Builds a rejection ThermalFitResult preserving counts, filter reasons, and fit window so the caller can distinguish 'no data', 'bad fit', and 'rejected by rule' uniformly.

nodes.name: rows_to_samples
nodes.summary: Converts Influx query rows to ThermalSample dataclasses; skips rows missing required telemetry and flags samples whose cool_setpoint_f moved >=0.5 F from the previous sample.

nodes.name: build_query
nodes.summary: Generates the Flux query that downsamples HVAC and ecowitt weather into aligned sample_minutes buckets and pivots into one wide row per timestamp (indoor/outdoor temps, solar, cool/heat actual %, cool setpoint).

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Argparse for the fit CLI: window-days, sample-minutes, min-samples, stage thresholds, and canonical outdoor measurement defaults (ecowitt.weather, ch1_temp_f, solar_wm2). --output-json and --dry-run are deprecated no-ops kept for operator-command stability.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: CLI entry point: validates required Influx env vars, builds the Flux query, opens InfluxDBClient (60s timeout), reads rows, fits the thermal model, prints a summary, and returns 0 only when intervals were produced.

nodes.name: _print_summary
nodes.summary: Human-readable summary printer for the fit result: accepted flag, tau, stage rates, solar coupling, intercept, RMSE/skill, sample counts, and the sorted filter_counts dict.

nodes.name: test_fit_rejects_holdout_skill_below_threshold

nodes.summary: Asserts fits outside FitConfig.tau_min_hours..tau_max_hours (2-48h) are rejected, blocking obviously broken building envelopes from feeding the scheduler.

nodes.name: comed_influx.py
nodes.summary: Converts a parsed ComEd Bill dataclass into InfluxDB line protocol (one comed.bill point plus N comed.bill_lineitems points) and writes the batch to InfluxDB v2. Timestamps anchor at 23:59:59 America/Chicago of the service_to date using a fixed CDT offset to dodge zoneinfo dependencies.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a fixed UTC offset rather than zoneinfo because the timestamp is a coarse end-of-period marker and dashboards bucket by day. Tag/field escaping is hand-rolled to keep the dependency surface minimal.

nodes.name: bill_to_line_protocol
nodes.summary: Serializes a Bill into a multi-line Influx line-protocol payload containing the rollup comed.bill measurement plus one comed.bill_lineitems measurement per LineItem, with tags for account_no, rate_plan, bill_type, category, and line_item.

nodes.name: write_bill
nodes.summary: Opens a synchronous InfluxDBClient, renders the Bill via bill_to_line_protocol, and writes the payload to the supplied bucket. Idempotency relies on Influx's natural upsert on (measurement, tag-set, timestamp).

nodes.summary: PJM Data Miner 2 poller service that fetches LMP, load, forecast and peak feeds on per-feed schedules and writes typed points to InfluxDB measurements consumed by the 5CP detector and analysis pipeline.
nodes.languageNotes: Async httpx client wrapped as an async context manager (PJMClient) with per-feed dispatcher table (FEED_DISPATCHERS) and FEED_SCHEDULE dataclass-driven gating; pure point-builder functions are factored out for unit testing.

nodes.name: Schedule

tour.title: Project Framing and Doc Map
tour.description: Start with README.md to learn what energy-proxy actually is: a Docker Compose stack on a Raspberry Pi that fuses ComEd Hourly Pricing, PJM 5CP risk, and NWS forecasts into HVAC setpoint decisions on an Amana CTK04AE thermostat. Then move to INDEX.md, the canonical doc map that groups every active document by intent — entry points, binding pre-registration, controller logic, telemetry, methodology, and ops. AGENTS.md gives you the standing rules every contributor (human or AI) follows, including the binding pre-registration constraint that freezes the field-study design at the OSF filing commit. Together these three documents tell you why this project exists and how to navigate the rest of the codebase.

tour.title: The Binding Pre-Registration Spec
tour.description: Every architectural decision downstream traces back to this single document. The SCED rebaseline spec defines the pre-registered field study comparing Arm A (the CTK04AE thermostat's programmed schedule) against Arm B (the active hvac-scheduler with RTP/DTOD/5CP-risk-aware rule-based control plus safety supervisor) starting June 1, 2026. Once filed to OSF, the hypotheses, arm definitions, arm calendar, metric definitions, statistical analysis plan, and decision rules are frozen at a commit hash — meaning the scheduler code, telemetry shape, and analysis pipeline you'll see in later steps are all subordinate to this text. PROJECT.md provides the historical narrative — how the project evolved from raw meter polling through 11 phases to the pre-registered study.

tour.title: The Deployment Stack
tour.description: With the why established, see the what. docker-compose.yml defines all 16 production services on Pi-lab — InfluxDB 2.7 (the single source of truth for telemetry), Grafana (the only visualization layer), the seven data ingest pollers, the HVAC scheduler and its watchdog, the Telegram notifier, and Loki/Promtail for log aggregation. SERVICES.md is the per-service operational reference that pairs every container with its purpose, port, and freshness contract. The energy-stack README is the operational guide of record: GitHub Actions + Tailscale deploy flow, docker compose ops cheat sheet, SOPS secret recovery, and the ComfortNet MQTT profile-gated services.
tour.languageLesson: Docker Compose service profiles (used here for the mqtt-gated mosquitto and telegraf services) let a single compose file describe multiple deployment modes — services without a profile always run, while profiled services activate only when their profile is explicitly requested via `--profile` or `COMPOSE_PROFILES`. Healthchecks expressed as `test:` commands with `interval`/`timeout`/`retries` drive container restart policy and tell the orchestrator when a service is actually serving traffic, not just running.

tour.title: The Data Ingest Layer
tour.description: Every decision in this system is downstream of telemetry, so the pollers come first. comed_poller fetches the ComEd Hourly Pricing API on a 5-minute cadence — this is the real-time price signal that drives the scheduler's scarcity-tier overlay. eagle_poller talks to the EAGLE-3 smart-meter gateway over LAN for whole-house electrical demand. pjm_dm2_poller (the highest-fan-in poller in the stack) fetches LMP, load, forecast, and peak feeds from PJM Data Miner 2 on per-feed schedules — these drive the 5CP risk classifier. All three write typed points to InfluxDB measurements with strict schema contracts.
tour.languageLesson: Each poller follows the same shape: an `async` loop that calls an external API, normalizes the response into Influx line-protocol Points, writes to the bucket, and touches `/tmp/last_poll_ok` so the Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK can verify freshness. The `last_poll_ok` mtime pattern is project-wide convention — every service uses it instead of HTTP health endpoints because pollers don't serve HTTP.

tour.title: The HVAC Scheduler Entry Point
tour.description: This is the heart of Arm B. hvac_scheduler/app.py is a persistent asyncio loop that decides each day's day-type (MILD / NORMAL / HOT_5CP_RISK / HOT_STREAK_DAY1) at 21:00 local from NWS, PJM, and ComEd Influx feeds, then pushes COOL_SETPOINT and HOLD_MODE commands to the Honeywell-based CTK04AE thermostat via Control4 Director. It also hosts the layer-priority resolver, safety-supervisor wiring, price-overlay state machine, and arm-calendar gating that locks Arm B writes to the 2026-06-01..2026-11-16 SCED window. HVAC_LOGIC.md is the canonical decision-flow reference — read it alongside the code, since the spec's controller constants are defined there.
tour.languageLesson: Python `asyncio` event loops keep the scheduler responsive while waiting on Influx queries and Control4 HTTP calls. The pattern here is a single top-level `async def main()` driving a `while True:` tick loop with `await asyncio.sleep(tick_interval)` — no thread pool, no multiprocess. State that must survive a restart is reconstructed from InfluxDB rather than held in process memory, which is what makes the scheduler safe to restart at any time.

tour.title: Scheduler Control Modules
tour.description: The scheduler's top-level app.py orchestrates these focused modules, which sit at BFS depth 1 — they're the direct dependencies that implement each piece of the control story. price_overlay.py implements the real-time scarcity-tier overlay (≥20¢/kWh maps to an 85F effective cool setpoint). precool.py decides when to pull setpoint down ahead of price spikes. pjm_5cp.py classifies whether tomorrow is at risk of being a PJM Five Coincident Peak day, which triggers the most aggressive avoidance schedule. safety_supervisor.py enforces hard limits on every command before it reaches the thermostat. freshness.py classifies upstream data ages against the locked Thresholds — and is the source-of-truth file paired with the cockpit copy enforced by the CI drift check.

tour.title: The Watchdog Safety Net
tour.description: A scheduler that can write to the thermostat is also a scheduler that can silently stop writing — so it gets a paired watchdog. hvac_scheduler_watchdog/check.py runs on its own schedule and alerts via Telegram when the scheduler's last-decision timestamp falls behind, when freshness inputs degrade, or when arm-calendar transitions don't fire as expected. ARM_TRANSITIONS.md documents the manual Monday arm-transition procedure (v1) for switching between Arm A and Arm B and the InfluxDB measurement schema for transitions. Together these enforce the resilience story: the field study cannot have undetected gaps in Arm B coverage, because that would invalidate the comparison against Arm A.

tour.title: The Cockpit Observability UI
tour.description: Grafana is the dashboards-of-record, but the Cockpit is the narrative observability layer Chris built for live debugging. The FastAPI backend exposes /api/snapshot, /api/day-ahead, /api/today-actions, and /api/day-at-a-glance — endpoints that route to canned fixtures or live assemblers based on COCKPIT_BACKEND_MODE. snapshot.py is the live-assembler that fuses raw thermostat, price, arm-mode, heartbeat, weather, day-type, and scheduler state into one snapshot DTO. The NarrativeCockpit React component renders that snapshot as a single-glance pane that explains what the scheduler is doing right now and why. Note the freshness.py copy here is the paired module enforced by the CI drift check from Step 6.

tour.title: The Offline SCED Analysis Pipeline
tour.description: The production stack produces telemetry; the analysis pipeline turns it into the pre-registered metrics. tools/analysis/pipeline.py is the 4692-line mega-module that runs Stages 1-9 of the SCED analysis — mode classification, weather vector construction, matching, baseline distribution, arm-period assembly, and the locked statistical analysis. replay/manifest.py defines the Manifest contract that pairs each measurement with its parquet file plus a SHA256 integrity hash, making every analysis run fully reproducible from a frozen dataset. REPLAY_VALIDATION.md formalizes the source-type catalog (observed_historical, observed_recent, weather_derived_compatibility, injected_validation_case) and the reason-coding rules that protect the pre-registered analysis from silent shape drift.

tour.title: CI/CD: Deploy, Validate, Type-Check
tour.description: The capstone shows how every change gets to Pi-lab and what gates protect the production stack along the way. deploy.yml is the canonical deploy: pushing to main with changes under deploy/** triggers a GitHub-hosted runner that joins the tailnet as an ephemeral tag:ci node, rsyncs the stack to Pi-lab over Tailscale SSH, runs docker compose build && up -d, and smoke-tests for restarting services. typecheck.yml is the branch-protected mypy gate. check-freshness-drift.yml is the bespoke PR guard that diffs the two parallel freshness.py modules (the hvac_scheduler canonical and the cockpit backend copy) and fails if they have drifted — enforcing the single-source-of-truth contract you saw in Steps 6 and 8. shadow-validation.yml is the manual-dispatch pre-experiment validation harness from Step 9 — it runs the analysis pipeline shape checks on the self-hosted Pi-lab runner before any new locked artifact gets blessed.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use `on:` triggers (push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch) and `jobs:` for parallelism. The ephemeral-tailnet-runner pattern here is unusual and worth noting: the deploy job authenticates to a private tailnet as a short-lived node using a one-off auth key, then uses Tailscale SSH to reach the Pi over a NAT'd home network without exposing any public ingress. The tag:ci ACL constrains what that ephemeral node can reach.
